findings.title: Update skips login-cache invalidation when the org-aware wrapper reports the IDP disabled
findings.body:
`update()` passes `idpById` to `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`. `idpById` comes from `getById()`, so it is wrapped by `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, and its `isEnabled()` returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled. The JPA `getForLogin` query does not look at organization state, so the cached login list can still contain this IDP's id.

Scenario:
1. The organization is disabled.
2. An admin sets `hideOnLogin=true` (or `linkOnly=true`) on one of its IDPs.
3. The original model fails the login predicate because the wrapper says disabled, and the updated model fails it because it is hidden. Both are false, so the method returns early and nothing is invalidated.
4. The organization is re-enabled. Organization updates do not invalidate the login keys.

The stale cached id is then resolved through `getById`. `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only re-checks `isEnabled()`, so the hidden or link-only IDP appears on the login page.

Fix: evaluate the predicate against the stored model without the wrapper (e.g. `idpDelegate.getById`). Alternatively, invalidate whenever any `LoginFilter` field or `BROKER_PUBLIC` changes.

findings.title: Cleanup registers removal of literal alias "alias" instead of created IDPs
findings.body:
`getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets an IDP named "alias", not the `idp-alias-N` providers this test creates. The same mistake is repeated at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`.

None of the 21 created IDPs are cleaned up. They leak into the realm for subsequent tests, which can change IDP counts and login-page results in other tests and cause order-dependent failures. Use the actual alias variable in the cleanup.
